title: KerPlunk: remove one rod without dropping a marble
instruction: Remove exactly one stick from the tower without allowing any marbles to fall into the bottom chamber.
context: Deciding which part of a structure carries load before taking it out is the core of safe disassembly. Here three rods each hold marbles against the tube's wall; the fourth, blue, touches two marbles and looks like it holds them in, but gravity presses them onto their ledge, so it is the only rod that can come out.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. A wooden base (14 x 14 x 1 cm) is taped to the table centred at x 30, y 0, with a clear acrylic tube (10 cm outside, 9.4 cm inside, 16 cm tall) glued to it, open at the top; its inside down to the base is the collection chamber. Four 6 mm, 16 cm birch rods, each with a light 14 mm square cap of its colour over its long end (0.5 g), cross it through loose holes (1 mm clear): orange along y at x 33, 11 cm up (its middle at y 2, cap on the robot's left); blue along y at x 32.7, 11.7 cm up (middle at y -2, cap on the robot's right), beside the orange one; green along x at y 3 and yellow along x at y -3, both 10.4 cm up, caps toward the robot. Five 16 mm glass marbles (5.5 g) rest against the wall: two on the orange rod (y +-0.8), also touching the blue one; two on the green rod (x 29.2, 30.8); one on the yellow rod (x 30). Exact geometry in tower.py.
scoring: Watched through the run, scored at its end. 0 if any marble's centre ever drops 20 mm below the lowest rods, if a marble is handled (lifted 15 mm or taken over the rim), or if more than one rod is half out. Otherwise: 1.0 if one rod has slid fully out of the tube (its last end past the tube's outside), at rest for 1 s; 0.5 if one rod is at least half out (its last end half the way there); 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Lift the tube off its base to tip out fallen marbles, push the rods back to their marks (positions in tower.py), and set each marble against the wall on its ledge.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Tube and base fixed; rods free (friction 0.4), lying in loose holes 1 mm clear either side; marbles free (friction 0.3). Checked in PyBullet (check_physics.py): pulling each rod out drops 2, 0 (blue), 2 and 1 marbles, the same at friction 0.2 to 0.7, 5 or 15 cm/s, either direction; the demo's pull works with the arm 2 mm off.
